title: FSM determinism, cache convergence, and declared coverage
purpose: Find reachable correctness failures where the same committed proposal and prior committed state can produce different apply results, cache state, audit evidence, or durable writes across replicas because apply depends on node-local state, undeclared reads, cache history, unsafe mutation, non-deterministic iteration, or storage reads. Apply the companion evidence and ownership contract; exclude accounting arithmetic, Raft quorum, persistence recovery, read projections, generic lifecycle, and API translation unless they are direct evidence for an apply/cache root cause.
invariants: Post-commit sentinel expectations must follow successful ordered effects, including same-proposal and cross-entry ledger deletion and ephemeral purge. Captured expectations must own reused WriteSet data; legitimate removal must not fail live apply or WAL replay, while missing or changed surviving volumes and any rows left by a deleted ledger's cascade must remain fatal, even if their aggregate is balanced or deletion is the only order in a batch.

For a fixed committed proposal, Raft index, and prior committed state, every replica and replay must produce the same apply outcome, audit bytes, counters, cache mutations, and durable writes. Wall clock, randomness, goroutine scheduling, map iteration, process identity, host resources, and node-local configuration must not affect that transition.

Lifecycle cleanup must derive its complete candidate set from proposal-declared coverage and committed state. A cleanup transition, skipped order, idempotent replay, or metadata-only operation must not delete an undeclared current row, omit a declared row, or change immutable history that the lifecycle contract retains.

Node-local flags, environment, startup settings, and binary defaults may gate admission before proposal, but apply must not consult them. A setting that affects committed semantics must arrive as ordered replicated input and be interpreted solely from committed state and proposal bytes.

Every cache-keyed read by an order, technical update, proposal-wide validation, or composed helper must be declared by its producer in plan.Coverage and represented by the correct per-operation coverage bits. Numscript discovery and all non-order producers must enrich or declare their own dependencies before Build; later phases must not widen the read horizon.

Every handler-side cache read must traverse processing.Scope and the state coverage gate before reaching an overlay or parent KeyStore. Raw WriteSet, DerivedRegistry, KeyStore, registry, parent reader, cache iterator, or equivalent capabilities must not be reachable from apply handlers in a way that bypasses the gate.

A missing, malformed, unknown, or out-of-range execution plan or coverage bit must fail through the documented deterministic rejection or invariant path before dependent mutation. Empty per-operation bits admit nothing and must not inherit proposal-wide or previous-operation coverage; proposal-wide scope is reserved for explicitly documented validations.

Apply must not read Pebble or any other node-local durable source. Its storage capability is write-only; all decision inputs come from the proposal, committed FSM state, scoped overlays, or correctly preloaded in-memory attributes. Recovery, synchronization, and admission reads must not leak a read capability into the hot path.

Creation of the apply path's main-store write capability is lifecycle-restricted. Apply handlers must receive only the existing scoped write path; they must not open their own dal.WriteSession, retain one across its owning batch, or add an OpenWriteSession call site without an explicitly justified lifecycle owner and the repository's static enforcement.

Admission Build, loader lifetime, predicted-index stamping, proposal guard, and generation-boundary rebuild must ensure that each committed plan supplies the values needed at its canonical cache horizon. A boundary crossing, delayed apply, concurrent preload, or loader release must not make the result depend on a node's incidental cache residency.

Generation selection and rotation depend only on the committed Raft index and replicated cluster policy. For the same applied index, replicas converge on equivalent Gen0/Gen1 contents, tombstones, tags, cache-mirror writes, and Bloom updates; entries are removed only by generation rotation.

MirrorPreload and in-batch overlays may seed or expose values only under their declared plan and must preserve later committed writes. Preload order, duplicate keys, Gen0/Gen1 residency, tombstones, Bloom readiness or false positives, and different cache histories must not alter business decisions or committed output.

Accepted order business payloads, including aliased maps, slices, protobuf messages, postings, metadata, and configuration, are immutable until their audit intent is captured. Planning, technical enrichment, apply, rollback, skip, and response construction may change only explicitly technical fields excluded by MarshalOrderBusinessIntent.

Failed, rejected, skipped, or impossible branches must leave exactly the documented effects. Temporary overlay mutations are discarded where required, a coverage miss occurs before the protected read or write, and contractually unreachable states surface loudly rather than silently returning, continuing, or committing a partial divergent prefix.

Adding or changing an attribute kind keeps canonical hashing, plan resolvers, coverage slots, gated accessors, preload loaders, cache and Bloom registries, persistence mirrors, and tests in lockstep. Unknown kinds or collision-tag mismatches cannot be interpreted differently according to local registry or cache state.

Coverage a producer derives from a read of state, rather than from request data, must bind that observation into the proposal and the apply path must re-derive it and reject a mismatch. Where the observation keys on a dependency the plan declares unconditionally — a revert's target state — the comparison must run before the dependent reads so a stale observation never reaches the coverage gate. Numscript is the one documented exception: its re-resolution may derive an account from changed metadata and perform the gated read before the inputs hash is compared, and that miss is intentionally left fatal (fsm/preload.md). Widening that exception, softening it into a retryable outcome, or adding a new read-derived declaration without both the binding and the ordering is a finding. A matching observation must never suppress a genuine under-declaration.

Audit-key initialization must use random bytes only before Raft proposal; apply and replay install the same first committed 32-byte secret on every replica, and every audited order uses that committed value independently of node-local cluster ID.

CreateLedger stages initial metadata in the canonical ledger-metadata keyspace in the same proposal as ledger identity, boundaries and initial schema. Committed metadata limits apply before staging; creation metadata requires no additional preload read and cannot mutate the audited order.

The FSM's Numscript artifact cache and its warm VM instances are node-local incidental state: the cache is sized by node-local configuration and its parsed/compiled residency, LRU eviction, cold decode+verify versus warm hit, entry replacement for different bytes under the same script hash, and an instance left dirty by a prior failed or panicking run must not change the outcome, audit bytes, or writes of a committed scripted order. A hit serves only the exact committed program bytes it verified, a reused verification record must not admit vars the program's layout does not cover, an instance never executes concurrently, and a completed run must not leave its store, Scope, or proposal plan reachable from the cache. A fully missing artifact (program, vars, and script hash all absent) is recompiled from the script text; a program alone absent, next to a present hash and vars, is also legitimate (admission may omit it once its own bookkeeping, NumscriptCache.SeenCompiledProgram, shows it already attached these exact bytes to an earlier proposal for this hash — a bounded LRU on admission's own cache instance, unrelated to and never informed by what any replica's apply-side cache actually holds; service protocol revision 23) and is served from this node's own apply-side cache or likewise recompiled from the text — both resolutions must reach byte-identical bytecode for the same hash, relying on the same per-library compile-determinism assumption the store checker's audit replay already makes, now also load-bearing on the live apply path. Any other partial artifact — a program present but truncated, with an invalid header, carrying a bytecode version the bundled library cannot read, or failing decode, verification, or the script-hash binding — fails the order with ErrNumscriptRuntime identically on every replica, and is never repaired from the text. The script hash keying the caches and binding the artifact is XXH3-128, not collision-resistant; that is accepted only while write scopes are cluster-wide.
adversarial_questions: For every production apply entry point and dispatched order or technical update, what exact values can influence branching and output? Can any call reach time.Now, timers, randomness, unordered map traversal, environment/configuration, host/process identity, mutable global state, or a node-local service?

Can two replicas starting from the same committed state but deliberately different flags, clocks, cache Gen0/Gen1 residency, Bloom readiness, preload timing, or loader completion produce different ApplyResult, audit encoding, WriteSet, counters, or cache state for identical proposal bytes and index?

For each processing.Scope Get method and every helper it calls, which producer declares the canonical key in plan.Coverage, which resolver builds it, which bit selects it, and which gated accessor checks it? Are dynamic Numscript dependencies, technical updates, mirror paths, and proposal-wide validations all covered?

For every lifecycle cleanup path, including state transitions, metadata-only orders, skipped orders, idempotent replays, and mirror ingestion, does the proposal declare the complete current-state candidate set? State-dependent enumeration may inspect persisted rows, but its trigger, cardinality, and cost must be explicit. Can cleanup delete an undeclared row, omit a declared row, or remove immutable history that the contract retains?

Can a handler retain a scope, accessor, LedgerInfo view, protobuf pointer, map, slice, or overlay from a prior operation and observe or mutate it after NewScope reuses backing storage? Can empty bits or a proposal-wide scope accidentally authorize a later per-order read?

Can a new attribute resolver, accessor, sub-attribute code, technical update, or direct Registry/KeyStore use be added on only one side of the declaration/enforcement matrix? What happens for an unknown attr code, malformed ID, duplicate plan, out-of-range bit, collision tag, or nil intent?

Does any apply-reachable concrete type, interface, closure, callback, iterator, or embedded field expose Pebble Get/NewIter or another local read source despite the nominal WriteSession boundary? Can error handling or a rare technical-update path escape that boundary?

Which lifecycle owner opens the main-store WriteSession used by apply, when is it closed, and can any order, technical update, helper, callback, or error path create or retain another session outside that batch boundary? Does every OpenWriteSession call site remain inside the statically enforced allowlist with a concrete lifecycle justification?

What happens when Build observes one generation and proposal assignment crosses one or several rotation boundaries, including guard rebuild failure, cancellation, leader change, delayed apply, duplicate preload entries, or early loader release? Is PredictedIndex verified against the actual apply index before mutation?

Can MirrorPreload overwrite a newer cache entry, resurrect a tombstone, trust a stale tag, or populate replicas differently when the same key is respectively absent, Gen0-resident, Gen1-resident, or concurrently written? Does put-if-absent preserve the canonical boundary semantics?

At rotation, are cache mutations, mirror rows, tombstones, Bloom dirty blocks, and generation metadata ordered so that every successful and failing prefix preserves cross-node equivalence? Can individual eviction, threshold change, snapshot installation, or recovery leave a different cache horizon at the next apply?

Can Bloom false negatives, stale readiness, configuration drift, restore, or follower synchronization suppress a required preload? Distinguish a performance-only false positive from a ready-but-incomplete filter that changes an apply decision.

Before and after coverage enrichment, planning, each order, skip rollback, technical updates, audit construction, and response creation, do MarshalOrderBusinessIntent bytes remain identical? Which clones establish ownership of nested maps, slices, messages, ledger configuration, postings, and metadata?

For every continue, nil return, fallback, recovered panic, ignored error, and partial Merge path in apply, is the state truly reachable and is the residual cache plus durable batch identical on all replicas? Does the test assertion uniquely exercise that branch rather than another rejection?

Do model, oracle, restart, divergence, coverage, aliasing, and rotation tests compare authoritative outputs and exact mutation sets across intentionally different local histories, or can they pass because all replicas share the same fixture state and configuration?

For each producer declaration derived from a read rather than from request data — a revert's volume keys come from the stored target, Numscript's from resolved balances/metadata — what happens when that read went stale before apply? Admission reads the local store with no read barrier, so a target committed but not yet applied there reads as absent and the order declares nothing. Is the observation bound and re-derived, does the comparison precede the dependent reads wherever the key is declared unconditionally, and where it cannot (Numscript) is the resulting gate-reaching read still documented and fatal rather than softened? Is the mismatch classified by whether re-admission can converge, can a permanently non-convergent case (a target the same batch creates) be returned as retryable, and does the comparison sit behind the handler's existing not-found/already-applied/invariant checks instead of overriding their reasons?
Can two leaders propose different initial audit keys or can an audited order overtake key initialization, causing replicas to hash under different values or append before durable key commit?

For normal and mirror creation, do rejection, proposal rollback and idempotent replay preserve initial metadata atomically without a second save, new metadata read dependency, duplicate allocation or order mutation?

For one committed scripted order, can two replicas whose Numscript caches differ — size, eviction, cold versus warm entry, an entry holding other compiled bytes for the same script hash, an instance dirtied by a prior error or recovered panic, a verification record produced by another order's vars — produce a different result, error classification, audit bytes, or writes? Does any present-but-unreadable or partial artifact reach recompilation from the text, does a missing one reach execution without the admission-bug signal outside audit replay, and does a completed run, including a panicking one, leave its store, Scope, or proposal plan reachable from a cached instance?

For a committed order whose compiled_program is absent next to a present compiled_vars and compiled_script_hash (admission's cache-based omission, service protocol revision 23), do a replica that hits its own cache for that hash and one that misses and recompiles from the script text converge on byte-identical bytecode, result, error classification, audit bytes, and writes? Does a malformed or wrong-length compiled_script_hash in this shape fail loudly rather than panic on the fixed-size conversion, and does the recompile path populate this node's cache so a later order on the same node also hits?
dynamic_checks_to_consider: Exercise transaction-then-DeleteLedger in one proposal, multiple entries, and separate commits with sentinel enabled. Include multiple deletion names to expose reused-slice aliasing, a surviving ledger with identical account/asset keys, deliberate missing/changed surviving rows, and balanced leftovers after a successful deletion in both mixed and deletion-only batches. Reopen WAL/Pebble and run Applier.RecoverAndReplay plus asynchronous follower catch-up; setup rejection or a disabled sentinel is not proof.

Inventory the production dispatch tables, processing.Scope reads, plan attr-code resolvers, state coverage slots/gated accessors, preload loaders, cache/Bloom registries, and protobuf oneofs. Build an exact declaration-to-enforcement matrix and reject a finding based only on a missing test or textual mismatch.

Use existing deterministic, model, oracle, coverage, cache-divergence, restart, aliasing, technical-update, and generation-boundary tests first. The audit may run allowed read-only or temporary diagnostics but must not edit tracked files; unexecuted scenarios remain reproduction plans.

Replay identical serialized proposals at identical indexes from cloned committed state while varying node-local configuration, clock sources, process environment, map insertion order, and cache Gen0/Gen1 placement; compare ApplyResult, audit bytes, counters, WriteSet/cache deltas, and persisted batch bytes.

For each operation type, instrument or wrap the scoped accessors in a temporary diagnostic to record actual cache-keyed reads, then compare them with the producer's plan.Coverage and encoded coverage bits. Exercise success, rejection, skip, intra-batch dependency, Numscript, mirror, and every TechnicalUpdate oneof.

Seed unrelated persisted rows, then admit the same ordinary write and compare the declared key count, serialized proposal size, and storage-read shape. Repeat with any operation that claims a wider lifecycle scope; if the candidate set or cost changes, the evidence must identify the explicit trigger and declared cardinality rather than treating the change as implicit.

Force Build immediately before a generation boundary, advance the index before guard acquisition, rebuild under the guard, delay committed apply, and vary loader release timing. Assert the stamped PredictedIndex, preloaded seed, final cache generations, audit result, and durable writes are identical across replicas.

Seed logically equivalent replicas with deliberately different incidental cache histories: key absent, Gen0, Gen1, tombstoned, duplicate preload, Bloom ready/not-ready and false-positive. Apply the same proposal and compare the complete observable transition, not only balances.

Exercise malformed and adversarial execution plans: empty bits, out-of-range bits, unknown attr codes, missing or non-16-byte IDs, duplicate plans, wrong intent, collision-tag mismatch, and undeclared dynamic reads. Verify deterministic failure before protected mutation and no inheritance from a prior scope.

Hash MarshalOrderBusinessIntent before and after conversion, coverage enrichment, Build, apply, rollback/skip, audit emission, and response construction using nested maps/slices/messages shared with the input. Mutate retained aliases in the diagnostic to prove whether ownership boundaries are real.

Statically inspect the apply-reachable dependency graph for read-capable DAL interfaces, Pebble Get/NewIter, direct parent registry/KeyStore access, time/random/config reads, and unordered iteration feeding persisted or audited output; confirm reachability and a concrete divergent state before reporting.

Inventory every OpenWriteSession call site and compare it with the repository's static allowlist. Trace the owning batch, close/error paths, and capabilities passed into apply handlers; distinguish a justified recovery or lifecycle writer from a new handler-reachable session grant.

Run the repository's focused race/model/oracle checks applicable at the audited SHA when their prerequisites are available. Record unavailable multi-node, restart, or instrumentation evidence as residual risk, not as a confirmed defect.
admit an order whose producer observed its dependency as absent, make that dependency present before apply, and verify the rejection happens before any dependent read and commits no mutation

Apply the same key-initialization proposal to isolated replicas, race a second distinct initialization, restart from each store, and compare persisted key and subsequent audit hashes at identical indexes; verify admission holds orders until key commit.

Execute the same committed scripted artifacts on caches with deliberately different histories — empty, warm, size 1 with interleaved scripts forcing eviction, an entry for the same script hash with other compiled bytes, and an instance left dirty by a preceding missing-funds failure and by a recovered store panic — and compare results, error reasons, and postings/metadata byte for byte. Start from TestSafeExecCompiled_* (WarmInstanceReuse, PanicLeavesInstanceReusable, SameScriptDifferentBytesRunsCommittedBytes, WarmHitForeignVersionRejected, WarmInstanceReleasesSource) and TestProduce_* (MissingArtifactRecompilesToTheSameOutcome, PartialArtifactIsLoud, InvalidArtifactHeaderIsLoud, UnreadableBytecodeVersionIsLoud), then hold a weak reference to the run's source to confirm a cached instance does not retain it after every exit path.
